items.headline: Cerebras's $25.4 billion backlog is nearly all OpenAI
items.why: A single OpenAI inference deal now accounts for the bulk of Cerebras's contracted revenue, meaning the AI-chip challenger's fortunes are tied almost entirely to one customer's future spending decisions.

sources.title: Cerebras Has a $25.4 Billion Backlog, and One OpenAI Agreement Is Behind Much of It

items.headline: Chinese AI chipmakers raise prices 20-50% as HBM costs bite
items.why: Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX have stopped competing on price against export-restricted Nvidia parts, confirmation that the memory shortage now sets a floor under AI compute costs everywhere, not just in the US.

sources.title: Morning Tech Digest, September 10, 2026: Chinese AI Chip Prices Up 20% to 50% on HBM Costs

items.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash on a new encoder-decoder architecture
items.why: A 552-billion-parameter model billed as DeepSeek's smallest signals the lab is optimizing for inference cost rather than chasing benchmarks, a sign Chinese labs are adapting to newly costlier domestic chips.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $77,000 as Iran war and rate-hike bets weigh
items.why: Bitcoin is down nearly 6% on the week and Fed rate-hike odds for the September meeting have jumped to 69%, showing crypto trading as a rate-sensitive risk asset rather than a safe haven during the Middle East escalation.

items.headline: Senate's CLARITY Act faces a make-or-break cloture vote September 15
items.why: Republicans need seven Democratic votes to even begin debate on the crypto market-structure bill, and unresolved fights over stablecoin yield and crypto-ethics rules make that math uncertain heading into the vote.

sources.title: CLARITY Act Fate Hinges on Senate Debate Vote

items.headline: Nasdaq invests $100 million in Kraken's parent at a $21 billion valuation
items.why: An incumbent exchange is now using a crypto venue as a retail distribution channel for tokenized stocks, the first arrangement of its kind with a major exchange's name attached rather than an offshore workaround.

items.headline: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia wound 73, hit oil facilities
items.why: The attacks mark a major escalation between an important US ally and Iran-backed rebels, threatening to squeeze a second shipping chokepoint just as the Strait of Hormuz war already curtails regional oil flows.

items.headline: US and Iran dig in for a 'protracted war' as fighting spreads to a second strait
items.why: Fighting around both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb picked up this week, with reporting that both sides are settling in for prolonged conflict, stretching the timeline over which the region's energy exports stay constrained.

items.headline: Fed rate-hike odds jump to 69% ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC meeting
items.why: Hot producer-price data pushed the odds of a hike higher in a single day, which would tighten financial conditions just as oil-driven inflation is already working through the economy.

items.why: Diesel is a key input for shipping, farming and construction, so a record price feeds directly into food and freight costs just as fall heating and harvest demand starts to climb.

items.why: The 400,000-barrel-a-day Jazan refinery went offline mid-attack, adding a second source of supply risk on top of the Strait of Hormuz disruptions already tightening global fuel markets.

items.why: Futures have surrendered 51% of the bounce from the September 2 low, and a sustained break below 7,680 versus a reclaim of 7,725-7,730 will decide whether this is just a correction or the start of something bigger.
